text.p01: To those who light up others, just like Lumi. A story about kindness and the gifts that grow when we share them.
text.p03: When the summer sun went down, the fireflies came out to dance. Blink! Blink! Blink!
text.p04: The smallest was Lumi, with the warmest glow. Her best friend, Moss the moth, couldn't glow at all, but he loved her light.
text.p05: One evening, Old Glow the glowworm called the whole meadow together.
text.p06: "The Night of No Moon is coming," she said. "It is the darkest night of all, and we will need every light."
text.p07: As the nights grew cooler, some fireflies' lights began to flicker… and fade.
text.p08: Lumi looked at her own glow and shivered. "What if my light runs out too?"
text.p09: So Lumi made a plan. She crawled into a hollow log and tucked her glow under a leaf.
text.p10: "Lumi, aren't you coming to dance?" Moss called. "Not tonight," she said. "I'm saving my light."
text.p11: Night after night, the meadow grew darker. Bump! The mouse family tripped over a stone.
text.p12: The snail lost the path home. Without the lights, everyone felt a little bit lost.
text.p13: Inside the log, Lumi's light was safe. But it was small, and it felt cold.
text.p14: All she could see was her own little glow, and the dark all around it.
text.p15: Then came the Night of No Moon. Moss flew out into the dark to look for his friend.
text.p16: But it was so dark that he flew in circles, and soon he was tangled in the brambles.
text.p17: "Lumi! Where are you?" His tiny voice drifted through the night.
text.p18: Lumi heard him. To help, she would have to go out and use her light. Her wings trembled.
text.p19: Lumi took a deep breath. She pulled off the leaf and flew out, shining.
text.p20: She found Moss in the brambles and lit the way, twig by twig, until he was free.
text.p21: Nearby, a little firefly sat alone. His light had gone out. "Can you help me?" he whispered.
text.p22: Lumi was afraid of losing more. But she gently touched her glow to his.
text.p23: Flicker… FLASH! His light bloomed, bright and golden.
text.p24: And Lumi's light didn't get smaller. It grew bigger and brighter than ever before!
text.p25: Together they lit another firefly, and another, and another.
text.p26: Soon a river of lights flowed across the whole meadow, like stars come down to play.
text.p27: Now the mouse family could see the stones. The snail found the path home.
text.p28: The lost duckling found her mother, and the hedgehog found his cozy nest.
text.p29: Old Glow smiled. "A light that is shared is never less. It is always more."
text.p30: So the cricket taught everyone his song, the hedgehog shared his nest with the chilly mice, and Old Glow told stories to the little ones.
text.p31: As the sun came up, Lumi and Moss rested on a dandelion, watching the lights blink off one by one.
text.p32: Some gifts grow bigger every time you give them away. The End
text.cover: The Light That Grows. A Story About Kindness and the Gifts That Grow When We Share Them
